          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now handle the `sessionFinishedMsg` and the `enter` key in `Update`:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_016w19gkbUDs4H15WRhxu8MX",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Handle session-finished message and the enter key to launch/attach a tmux session.",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"left\", \"h\", \"shift+tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"right\", \"l\", \"tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Move within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// launchSelectedRepo starts (or attaches to) the tmux session for the repo\n// under the cursor, handing the terminal to tmux via tea.ExecProcess. The\n// bubbletea program is suspended while tmux runs and resumes on exit.\nfunc (m model) launchSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos || len(m.repoAliases) == 0 {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\n\talias := m.repoAliases[m.repoCursor]\n\trepo := repos.Find(alias)\n\tif repo == nil {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Decide whether to create+attach (first launch) or just attach\n\t// (session already exists from a previous launch this run).\n\tvar cmd *exec.Cmd\n\tif repo.Session == nil {\n\t\trepo.Session = session.New()\n\t\tcmd = commands.CreateSession(repo.Session.ID, repo.Path)\n\t} else {\n\t\tcmd = commands.AttachToSession(repo.Session.ID)\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, tea.ExecProcess(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {\n\t\treturn sessionFinishedMsg{err: err}\n\t})\n}",
                "oldStr": "func (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"left\", \"h\", \"shift+tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"right\", \"l\", \"tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Move within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}",
                "path": "/Users/egriham/repos/misc/taco/ui/ui.go"
              }

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds and vets cleanly. Here's what pressing Enter now does:\n\n1. Finds the repo under the cursor via `repos.Find(alias)`.\n2. If the repo has no session yet (`repo.Session == nil`), it creates one (`session.New()`, generating a unique ID) and runs your original `CREATE_SESSION_COMMAND` (which creates *and* attaches). If a session already exists, it runs `ATTACH_SESSION_COMMAND` instead.\n3. Runs that command through **`tea.ExecProcess`**, which suspends the bubbletea UI, hands the full terminal over to tmux (so all your escape/mouse bindings and `zsh` work normally), and resumes the UI when you detach.\n4. On resume, any error is captured and shown in the footer.\n\nAll your special command arguments are preserved verbatim — the only change in `commands.go` was running through `sh -c` so the shell actually interprets them.\n\nImportant caveat: **I verified this compiles and vets, but I could not run it**, because tmux takes over a real TTY and there's no interactive terminal available to me here. This is the kind of code that needs a live run to confirm behavior. Please test it:\n\n```\ngo run .\n```\n\nThen, on the Repos tab, move to a repo and press Enter. Things to watch for:\n- Whether you drop into a tmux session rooted at the repo's path.\n- Whether detaching (your Escape binding) returns you cleanly to the taco UI.\n- Whether `sh -c` correctly parses the multi-line script (if tmux complains about syntax, the line-continuation backslashes inside the Go raw string may need adjustment — tell me the exact error and I'll fix it).\n\nOne design note for later: the `repo.Session` is in-memory only, so it resets each time you restart taco. If you want taco to reattach to sessions that survived a restart, we'd persist the session ID and check `tmux has-session` on launch. Want me to add that, or test the current flow first?"

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Two design points before coding, because they affect correctness:\n\n**1. SIGINT and bubbletea overlap.** Your UI already maps `ctrl+c` to `tea.Quit`, and bubbletea *also* installs its own signal handler for SIGINT by default — it catches the signal and quits the program gracefully, so `program.Run()` returns normally. That means in the normal case, Ctrl+C won't reach a `signal.Notify` handler in `main` as a raw signal; bubbletea intercepts it and just returns. So the reliable place to do cleanup is **after `program.Run()` returns**, not (only) in a signal handler. A `defer cleanup()` in `main` covers both normal quit and Ctrl+C.\n\n**2. But `defer` won't run on a hard kill or `os.Exit`.** If the process is killed with SIGTERM/SIGKILL, or if some path calls `os.Exit`, deferred functions don't run. So the robust approach is *both*:\n   - a `defer cleanup()` for the normal/Ctrl+C path, guarded so it only runs once, and\n   - a `signal.Notify` handler for SIGINT/SIGTERM that runs cleanup and then exits — as a backstop for signals that arrive outside bubbletea's handling (e.g. SIGTERM, which bubbletea does not catch).\n\n**3. I need a way to enumerate sessions.** The `repos` package has no accessor that returns repos with live sessions. Cleanest is to add a small helper in `repos` (it owns `Instance`). I'll add `WithSessions()` returning repos whose `Session != nil`.\n\nLet me add that accessor first:"

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds and vets cleanly. The cleanup covers three exit paths:\n\n1. **Normal quit / Ctrl+C** — bubbletea catches SIGINT itself and returns from `program.Run()`, so `defer terminateAllSessions()` handles both. This is the common case.\n2. **SIGTERM (and SIGINT outside the UI loop)** — a `signal.Notify` goroutine runs cleanup and exits, as a backstop for signals bubbletea doesn't consume.\n3. **Run error** — cleanup runs explicitly before exiting.\n\nA `sync.Once` guards `terminateAllSessions` so it runs at most once even if two paths fire (e.g. signal handler + defer). It iterates `repos.WithSessions()` (the new accessor returning repos with `Session != nil`) and runs your `TERMINATE_SESSION_COMMAND` for each.\n\nTwo honest caveats:\n\n- **I can't run this** — it needs a real TTY and tmux, which I don't have here. Please test: launch a session with Enter, detach, then quit taco (both `q` and Ctrl+C), and verify with `tmux ls` that the session is gone.\n- **One race worth knowing:** the signal goroutine calls `os.Exit(1)` immediately after cleanup. If a signal arrives *while you're attached inside tmux*, bubbletea is suspended (via `ExecProcess`) and the signal behavior gets murkier — the signal may go to tmux/the foreground process group rather than taco. In practice Ctrl+C while inside tmux goes to whatever's running in the tmux pane, not taco, so this mainly matters for an external `kill`. That's an edge case; the primary quit-from-UI path is solid.\n\nThere's also a limitation inherent to the approach: `SIGKILL` (`kill -9`) and power loss can never be trapped, so a session could survive those. If you want taco to clean up *orphaned* sessions from a previous run, that needs the persisted-session-ID approach I mentioned earlier (check `tmux has-session` at startup and reap stragglers). Want me to add that, or is trapping the normal exit paths enough for now?"
          }

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Here's a design consideration first: right now the model stores `repoAliases []string`, which is a static snapshot taken once at startup. It has no idea which repos have active sessions, and it can't sort by session state because it only holds alias strings. So to do this properly, the Repos tab needs to work from the live `*repos.Repo` list, not a cached alias slice — that way \"active\" reflects the current `Session` field and ordering can react to it.\n\nThe cleanest approach: build the ordered list at render time from `repos.WithSessions()` + the rest, so active sessions float to the top with an indicator, and it stays correct as sessions start/stop.\n\nLet me look at the current model/render code to refactor it:"

    {
      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "ToolResults",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "71e50653-6d5f-41c3-9c88-69e6f2dd1989",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "toolResult",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01EoKXaKnEG7XHQA7852sxqe",
              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\n\ttea \"charm.land/bubbletea/v2\"\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/commands\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/repos\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/session\"\n)\n\n// Tab identifies a top-level view in the UI.\ntype Tab int\n\nconst (\n\tTabRepos Tab = iota\n\tTabChats\n\tTabComingSoon\n)\n\n// tabTitles are the labels shown in the tab bar, in order.\nvar tabTitles = []string{\"Repos\", \"Chats\", \"Coming Soon\"}\n\n// sessionFinishedMsg is sent when a tmux session (run via tea.ExecProcess)\n// exits and the bubbletea program resumes.\ntype sessionFinishedMsg struct {\n\terr error\n}\n\ntype model struct {\n\tactiveTab Tab\n\n\t// Terminal dimensions, updated on every resize.\n\twidth  int\n\theight int\n\n\t// Repos tab state.\n\trepoAliases []string\n\trepoCursor  int\n\n\t// lastErr holds the most recent session error, shown in the footer.\n\tlastErr error\n}\n\nfunc initialModel() model {\n\treturn model{\n\t\tactiveTab:   TabRepos,\n\t\trepoAliases: repos.Aliases(),\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Init() tea.Cmd {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"left\", \"h\", \"shift+tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"right\", \"l\", \"tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Move within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// launchSelectedRepo starts (or attaches to) the tmux session for the repo\n// under the cursor, handing the terminal to tmux via tea.ExecProcess. The\n// bubbletea program is suspended while tmux runs and resumes on exit.\nfunc (m model) launchSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos || len(m.repoAliases) == 0 {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\n\talias := m.repoAliases[m.repoCursor]\n\trepo := repos.Find(alias)\n\tif repo == nil {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Decide whether to create+attach (first launch) or just attach\n\t// (session already exists from a previous launch this run).\n\tvar cmd *exec.Cmd\n\tif repo.Session == nil {\n\t\trepo.Session = session.New()\n\t\tcmd = commands.CreateSession(repo.Session.ID, repo.Path)\n\t} else {\n\t\tcmd = commands.AttachToSession(repo.Session.ID)\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, tea.ExecProcess(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {\n\t\treturn sessionFinishedMsg{err: err}\n\t})\n}\n\n// nextTab / prevTab cycle through the tabs.\nfunc (m model) nextTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) + 1) % len(tabTitles))\n}\n\nfunc (m model) prevTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) -           {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds and vets cleanly. (Go doesn't error on unused *exported* functions or unused package-level functions, so `Row` and `repos.Aliases`/`repos.Find` remain without breaking the build — they're just not called from the repos flow anymore. I left them in place since they're harmless and `Find` is still a reasonable public accessor.)\n\nWhat changed:\n\n- **Single source of truth for ordering** — `orderedRepos()` computes the display list each time: repos with a live `Session` first (alphabetical), then inactive repos (alphabetical). The cursor, rendering, and launch all use it, so they never disagree.\n- **Active indicator** — `RepoRow` shows a green `●` next to repos with a running session, a blank for the rest, plus the `›` cursor marker for the selected row.\n- **Live data** — the model no longer caches a static `repoAliases` snapshot; it reads `repos.All()` at render time, so as sessions start/stop the list reorders and the indicators update automatically.\n\nBehavior note worth flagging: when you start a session and return to the UI, that repo jumps to the top. Since the cursor is a positional index, it will now point at whatever repo landed at that position — the cursor doesn't \"follow\" the repo you just launched. If you'd prefer the cursor to stay on the same repo across reordering (track by alias instead of index), I can change that. Otherwise this is the common behavior.\n\nAs before: I verified compile + vet, but the interactive tmux behavior needs a real terminal — please run `go run .`, launch a session, detach, and confirm the launched repo shows the green `●` and sits at the top. Want me to make the cursor follow the selected repo across reordering?"
          }
        ]
      }
    },

Let me wire that in.\n\nFirst, add a field to remember the launched alias:"

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "There's a subtlety with mutating `m` here: `launchSelectedRepo` has a value receiver `(m model)` and returns `m`, so the mutation is preserved through the return. Good. Now handle the cursor-follow when the session finishes:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01U1tymjrbT1gr43qHzV8of9",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "On session finish, move the cursor to the launched repo's new position.",
                "command": "strReplace",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds and vets cleanly. Now when you press Enter on a repo, `launchSelectedRepo` records its alias. When you detach and the UI resumes (`sessionFinishedMsg`), it finds that repo's new index in the reordered list and moves the cursor there — so the cursor lands on the repo you just launched, which is now at the top.\n\nSince the newly-launched repo sorts to the top of the active group alphabetically, in the common case the cursor will end up at (or near) index 0, right on the session you started.\n\nVerify with a real run (`go run .`): start a session, detach, and confirm the cursor is now sitting on that repo at the top rather than stuck at the old position."
          }
        ]
      }

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Right now the indicator sits on the left. To move it to the right and align it in a column 5 spaces past the longest alias, `RepoRow` needs to know the longest alias width — it can't compute that per-row in isolation. So I'll pass the column width in from the caller (which sees all repos) and pad each alias to that width + 5 before appending the indicator.\n\nLet me update `renderReposTab` to compute the max alias length and pass it through:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01PVSD6AY5opZ53WCpht39uc",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Compute the longest alias and pass an indicator column position into RepoRow.",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos()\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}",
                "oldStr": "// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos()\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}",
                "path": "/Users/egriham/repos/misc/taco/ui/ui.go"
              }
            }
          }

Because the column is computed from the longest alias across all rows, every indicator lines up in the same vertical column.\n\nSo a list like:\n\n```\n  api            ●\n  web-dashboard  ●\n  tools\n```\n\nwith the dots aligned 5 spaces past the longest alias (`web-dashboard`).\n\nTwo caveats worth noting:\n- The alignment uses `len(alias)`, which counts bytes, not display width. For plain ASCII aliases that's identical to visible width.                   "data": "func Row(text string, selected bool) string {\n\tif selected {\n\t\treturn selectedRowStyle.Render(\"› \" + text)\n\t}\n\treturn rowStyle.Render(\"  \" + text)\n}\n\n// activeIndicatorStyle marks repos with a running session.\nvar activeIndicatorStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().\n\tBold(true).\n\tForeground(lipgloss.Color(\"42\")) // green\n\n// RepoRow renders a repo menu row with a cursor marker on the left and an\n// active-session indicator aligned to indicatorCol on the right. indicatorCol\n// is the column (measured from the start of the alias) where the indicator\n// is drawn, so all indicators line up regardless of alias length.\nfunc RepoRow(alias string, indicatorCol int, active, selected bool) string {\n\tcursor := \"  \"\n\tif selected {\n\t\tcursor = \"› \"\n\t}\n\n\t// Pad the alias out to the indicator column so the indicator aligns.\n\tpad := indicatorCol - len(alias)\n\tif pad < 1 {\n\t\tpad = 1\n\t}\n\tpadding := strings.Repeat(\" \", pad)\n\n\tindicator := \" \"\n\tif active {\n\t\tindicator = activeIndicatorStyle.Render(\"●\")\n\t}\n\n\tline := cursor + alias + padding + indicator\n\tif selected {\n\t\treturn selectedRowStyle.Render(line)\n\t}\n\treturn rowStyle.Render(line)\n}"

              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "\n// Panel wraps content in a bordered box sized to the given width/height.\n// When width/height are <= 0 the panel sizes to its content.\nfunc Panel(content string, width, height int) string {\n\ts := panelStyle\n\tif width > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and horizontal padding (4).\n\t\ts = s.Width(width - 2)\n\t}\n\tif height > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and vertical padding (2).\n\t\ts = s.Height(height - 2)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(content)\n}\n\n// Help renders footer help text in a muted style.\nfunc Help(text string) string {\n\treturn helpStyle.Render(text)\n}\n\n// Center places content in the middle of the given box.\nfunc Center(width, height int, content string) string {\n\tif width <= 0 || height <= 0 {\n\t\treturn content\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.Place(width, height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, content)\n}\n\n// muted is a small helper for dimming arbitrary text."
                }
              ],
              "status": "success"
            }

                    "Text": "\n// Panel wraps content in a bordered box sized to the given width/height.\n// When width/height are <= 0 the panel sizes to its content.\nfunc Panel(content string, width, height int) string {\n\ts := panelStyle\n\tif width > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and horizontal padding (4).\n\t\ts = s.Width(width - 2)\n\t}\n\tif height > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and vertical padding (2).\n\t\ts = s.Height(height - 2)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(content)\n}\n\n// Help renders footer help text in a muted style.\nfunc Help(text string) string {\n\treturn helpStyle.Render(text)\n}\n\n// Center places content in the middle of the given box.\nfunc Center(width, height int, content string) string {\n\tif width <= 0 || height <= 0 {\n\t\treturn content\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.Place(width, height, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, content)\n}\n\n// muted is a small helper for dimming arbitrary text."
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "I see a pre-existing sizing inconsistency in `Panel`: with Lip Gloss, `.Width()` sets the *content* width (padding and border add on top). So `s.Width(width-2)` plus border(2)+padding(4) actually renders wider than `width`. The comments even say \"border (2) and horizontal padding (4)\" but the code only subtracts 2. This means the panel likely already overflows slightly — but you haven't reported that, so either your terminal is wide enough that it's not obvious or Lip Gloss is clamping. I'll fix the math while I'm here so centering lands correctly.\n\nThe correct inner content dimensions are:\n- inner width = `width - 2 (border) - 4 (padding L+R)`\n- inner height = `height - 2 (border) - 2 (padding T+B)`\n\nI'll have `Panel` set `.Width`/`.Height` to those inner values, and add the centering by placing the content into that same inner box. Cleanest: a `PanelCentered` variant, or a flag. I'll add a dedicated helper so the plain `Panel` stays available."
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01Xge97rBqhisTZDKNivC38J",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Fix panel inner sizing and add a centered-content panel helper.",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "// Panel border + padding costs, used to compute the inner content area.\nconst (\n\tpanelBorderW  = 2 // left + right border\n\tpanelBorderH  = 2 // top + bottom border\n\tpanelPaddingW = 4 // left + right padding (2 each)\n\tpanelPaddingH = 2 // top + bottom padding (1 each)\n)\n\n// panelInner returns the content area (width, height) available inside a panel\n// of the given outer width/height, after border and padding.\nfunc panelInner(width, height int) (int, int) {\n\treturn width - panelBorderW - panelPaddingW, height - panelBorderH - panelPaddingH\n}\n\n// Panel wraps content in a bordered box sized to the given width/height.\n// When width/height are <= 0 the panel sizes to its content.\nfunc Panel(content string, width, height int) string {\n\ts := panelStyle\n\tif width > 0 {\n\t\ts = s.Width(width - panelBorderW - panelPaddingW)\n\t}\n\tif height > 0 {\n\t\ts = s.Height(height - panelBorderH - panelPaddingH)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(content)\n}\n\n// PanelCentered wraps content in a bordered box like Panel, but centers the\n// content both horizontally and vertically within the panel's inner area.\nfunc PanelCentered(content string, width, height int) string {\n\tif width <= 0 || height <= 0 {\n\t\treturn Panel(content, width, height)\n\t}\n\tinnerW, innerH := panelInner(width, height)\n\tcentered := lipgloss.Place(innerW, innerH, lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center, content)\n\treturn Panel(centered, width, height)\n}",
                "oldStr": "// Panel wraps content in a bordered box sized to the given width/height.\n// When width/height are <= 0 the panel sizes to its content.\nfunc Panel(content string, width, height int) string {\n\ts := panelStyle\n\tif width > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and horizontal padding (4).\n\t\ts = s.Width(width - 2)\n\t}\n\tif height > 0 {\n\t\t// Account for the border (2) and vertical padding (2).\n\t\ts = s.Height(height - 2)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(content)\n}",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds and vets cleanly. The list (and the placeholder text on the other tabs) is now centered both horizontally and vertically inside the panel via `PanelCentered`, which uses `lipgloss.Place` within the panel's inner area.\n\nI also fixed a latent sizing bug while I was in there: the old `Panel` subtracted only `2` from the width but the box actually costs border(2) + padding(4) horizontally, so it was rendering wider than intended (likely overflowing on narrower terminals). `Panel` now computes the true inner content area, and `panelInner` centralizes that math so `PanelCentered` places content into the exact available space.\n\nOne thing worth deciding: the whole list block is centered as a unit, so the list stays left-aligned *within itself* (rows share a left edge) but the block sits in the middle of the box. That's usually what \"list in the middle\" means and keeps the indicator column alignment intact. If instead you wanted each row individually centered, that would break the indicator column — so I went with block-centering. \n\nVerify with `go run .` since I can't render it. Want the tab body vertically centered only (list kept at the left margin horizontally), or is fully-centered as-is what you're after?"
          }
        ]

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Short answer: no — a terminal program can't change font size. Text size is controlled entirely by the user's terminal emulator (iTerm2, Alacritty, etc.) and their font settings, not by anything the program can emit. There's no escape sequence or Lip Gloss option for \"bigger text\" the way there is for color or bold. So bubbletea/Lip Gloss fundamentally can't do it.\n\nWhat you *can* do to make things read as bigger or bolder within those constraints:\n\n1. **Bold** — you're already using it on active tabs and selected rows. It's the closest thing to \"heavier\" text.\n\n2. **FIGlet-style ASCII banners** — render text as large multi-line glyphs built out of regular characters. This is how CLI tools show big titles. Charm has a library for exactly this that pairs with your v2 stack. It only makes sense for short strings (a title, a logo, maybe a single selected item), not a whole scrollable list — a repo list rendered in giant letters would overflow instantly.\n\n3. **A minor terminal trick:** some terminals support a \"double-height line\" DEC escape (`ESC # 3` / `ESC # 4`), but support is spotty (works in xterm, not in many modern emulators) and Lip Gloss doesn't manage it, so it's fragile. I wouldn't rely on it.\n\nLet me check whether the big-text library is available in your module cache so option 2 is actually on the table:"
          },
          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01JCmTwagtyG9knKZijgDnkH",
              "name": "shell",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Good feature. Let me think through the design before coding, because a search box changes how key input is routed.\n\nThe key tension: right now single letters like `h`, `j`, `k`, `l`, `q` are navigation/quit shortcuts. Once there's a search box, typed letters must go into the query instead — otherwise you can't search for a repo containing \"q\". So I need to rethink key handling:\n\n- **Typed characters** (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, etc.) → append to the search query.\n- **Backspace** → delete last char.\n- **Arrow keys** (`↑`/`↓`) → navigate the filtered list (not `j`/`k`, since those are now search input).\n- **Tab / Shift+Tab** (or `←`/`→`) → switch tabs. I'll keep arrows for tabs too, but arrows are also list nav... conflict. I'll use **Tab/Shift+Tab for tab switching** and **arrows for list navigation**, freeing letters for search.\n- **Ctrl+C** → quit (can't type Ctrl+C into a search box anyway). Drop `q` as quit since it's now a searchable char.\n- **Enter** → launch selected repo (unchanged).\n- **Esc** → clear the search query (nice touch).\n\nFiltering: case-insensitive substring match on the alias, applied on top of the existing active-first ordering.\n\nLet me look at the current `View` layout and the ordering/nav code to wire this in."
          },

              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01VESxnDfJbyDjcx5kLcpXsF",
              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\n\ttea \"charm.land/bubbletea/v2\"\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/commands\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/repos\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/session\"\n)\n\n// Tab identifies a top-level view in the UI.\ntype Tab int\n\nconst (\n\tTabRepos Tab = iota\n\tTabChats\n\tTabComingSoon\n)\n\n// tabTitles are the labels shown in the tab bar, in order.\nvar tabTitles = []string{\"Repos\", \"Chats\", \"Coming Soon\"}\n\n// sessionFinishedMsg is sent when a tmux session (run via tea.ExecProcess)\n// exits and the bubbletea program resumes.\ntype sessionFinishedMsg struct {\n\terr error\n}\n\ntype model struct {\n\tactiveTab Tab\n\n\t// Terminal dimensions, updated on every resize.\n\twidth  int\n\theight int\n\n\t// Repos tab state.\n\trepoCursor int\n\n\t// launchedAlias is the repo whose session was most recently launched,\n\t// so the cursor can follow it after the list reorders.\n\tlaunchedAlias string\n\n\t// lastErr holds the most recent session error, shown in the footer.\n\tlastErr error\n}\n\nfunc initialModel() model {\n\treturn model{\n\t\tactiveTab: TabRepos,\n\t}\n}\n\n// orderedRepos returns the repos in display order: active sessions first\n// (alphabetical), then the rest (alphabetical). This is the single source of\n// truth for the Repos tab, so the cursor index, rendering, and launch all\n// agree on the same ordering.\nfunc orderedRepos() []*repos.Repo {\n\tall := repos.All()\n\n\tactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tinactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tfor _, r := range all {\n\t\tif r.Session != nil {\n\t\t\tactive = append(active, r)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tinactive = append(inactive, r)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tbyAlias := func(list []*repos.Repo) {\n\t\tsort.Slice(list, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\t\treturn list[i].Alias < list[j].Alias\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tbyAlias(active)\n\tbyAlias(inactive)\n\n\treturn append(active, inactive...)\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Init() tea.Cmd {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos() {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"left\", \"h\", \"shift+tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"right\", \"l\", \"tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Move within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// launchSelectedRepo starts (or attaches to) the tmux session for the repo\n// under the cursor, handing the terminal to tmux via tea.ExecProcess. The\n// bubbletea program is suspended while tmux runs and resumes on exit.\nfunc (m model) launchSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tordered := orderedRepos()\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos || len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\tif m.repoCursor >= len(ordered) {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = len(ordered) - 1\n\t}\n\n\trepo := ordered[m.repoCursor]\n\n\t// Remember which repo we launched so the cursor can follow it to its\n\t// new position once the list reorders on return.\n\tm.launchedAlias = repo.Alias\n\n\t// Decide whether to create+attach (first launch) or just attach\n\t// (session already exists from a previous launch this run).\n\tvar cmd *exec.Cmd\n\tif repo.Session == nil {\n\t\trepo.Session = session.New()\n\t\tcmd = commands.CreateSession(repo.Session.ID, repo.Path)\n\t} else {\n\t\tcmd = commands.AttachToSession(repo.Session.ID)\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, tea.ExecProcess(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {\n\t\treturn sessionFinishedMsg{err: err}\n\t})\n}\n\n// nextTab / prevTab cycle through the tabs.\nfunc (m model) nextTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) + 1) % len(tabTitles))\n}\n\nfunc (m model) prevTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) - 1 + len(tabTitles)) % len(tabTitles))\n}\n\n// moveCursor adjusts the cursor for whichever tab is active.\nfunc (m *model) moveCursor(delta int) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcount := len(orderedRepos())\n\tnext := m.repoCursor + delta\n\tif next >= 0 && next < count {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = next\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m model) View() tea.View {\n\t// Tab bar across the top.\n\ttabBar := TabBar(tabTitles, int(m.activeTab))\n\n\t// Body for the active tab.\n\tvar body string\n\tswitch m.activeTab {\n\tcase TabRepos:\n\t\tbody = m.renderReposTab()\n\tcase TabChats:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Chats\")\n\tcase TabComingSoon:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Coming Soon\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Wrap the body in a bordered panel that fills the window (minus the\n\t// tab bar and footer rows), with the content centered inside.\n\tpanelHeight := m.height - 4 // tab bar (1) + blank (1) + footer (2)\n\tpanel := PanelCentered(body, m.width, panelHeight)\n\n\tfooter := Help(\"←/→ switch tabs · ↑/↓ navigate · enter open · q quit\")\n\tif m.lastErr != nil {\n\t\tfooter = Help(\"session error: \"+m.lastErr.Error()) + \"\\n\" + footer\n\t}\n\n\tcontent := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, tabBar, panel, footer)\n\n\t// Take over the whole terminal window.\n\tv := tea.NewView(content)\n\tv.AltScreen = true\n\treturn v\n}\n\n// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos()\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}\n\n// renderPlaceholder is shown for tabs with no content yet.\nfunc (m model) renderPlaceholder(name string) string {\n\treturn muted(name + \" — nothing here yet.\")\n}\n\nfunc CreateProgram() *tea.Program {\n\treturn tea.NewProgram(initialModel())\n}"

4 // tab bar (1) + blank (1) + footer (2)\n\tpanel := PanelCentered(body, m.width, panelHeight)\n\n\tfooter := Help(\"←/→ switch tabs · ↑/↓ navigate · enter open · q quit\")\n\tif m.lastErr != nil {\n\t\tfooter = Help(\"session error: \"+m.lastErr.Error()) + \"\\n\" + footer\n\t}\n\n\tcontent := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, tabBar, panel, footer)\n\n\t// Take over the whole terminal window.\n\tv := tea.NewView(content)\n\tv.AltScreen = true\n\treturn v\n}\n\n// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos()\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}\n\n// renderPlaceholder is shown for tabs with no content yet.\nfunc (m model) renderPlaceholder(name string) string {\n\treturn muted(name + \" — nothing here yet.\")\n}\n\nfunc CreateProgram() *tea.Program {\n\treturn tea.NewProgram(initialModel())\n}"

            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now rewrite the key handling: arrows only for navigation, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+Q to quit, typed runes into the query, backspace/esc for editing. bubbletea v2's `KeyPressMsg` exposes the typed text — let me handle both named keys and printable input. I'll use `msg.String()` for named keys and check for single printable characters."

            "data": {

              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Replace key handling: arrows navigate, ctrl+c/ctrl+q quit, typed runes feed the search box, backspace/esc edit it.",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos(m.query) {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"ctrl+q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"shift+tab\", \"left\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"tab\", \"right\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Navigate within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\n\t\t// Clear the search query.\n\t\tcase \"esc\":\n\t\t\tm.setQuery(\"\")\n\n\t\t// Delete the last search character.\n\t\tcase \"backspace\":\n\t\t\tif m.query != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query[:len(m.query)-1])\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Any single printable character is typed into the search box.\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tif s := msg.String(); len(s) == 1 && s[0] >= 0x20 && s[0] < 0x7f {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query + s)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// setQuery updates the search query and resets the cursor to the top of the\n// filtered list so the selection stays valid.\nfunc (m *model) setQuery(q string) {\n\tm.query = q\n\tm.repoCursor = 0\n}",
                "oldStr": "\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos() {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"left\", \"h\", \"shift+tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"right\", \"l\", \"tab\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Move within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\", \"k\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\", \"j\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}",

                    "newStr": "\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos(m.query) {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"ctrl+q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"shift+tab\", \"left\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"tab\", \"right\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Navigate within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\n\t\t// Clear the search query.\n\t\tcase \"esc\":\n\t\t\tm.setQuery(\"\")\n\n\t\t// Delete the last search character.\n\t\tcase \"backspace\":\n\t\t\tif m.query != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query[:len(m.query)-1])\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Any single printable character is typed into the search box.\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tif s := msg.String(); len(s) == 1 && s[0] >= 0x20 && s[0] < 0x7f {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query + s)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// setQuery updates the search query and resets the cursor to the top of the\n// filtered list so the selection stays valid.\nfunc (m *model) setQuery(q string) {\n\tm.query = q\n\tm.repoCursor = 0\n}",

                }
              ],
              "status": "success"

When the query\n// is empty a muted placeholder is shown.\nfunc SearchBox(query string, width int) string {\n\tprompt := searchPromptStyle.Render(\"🔍 \")\n\n\tvar text string\n\tif query == \"\" {\n\t\ttext = muted(\"search…\")\n\t} else {\n\t\ttext = query + \"▏\" // simple block cursor\n\t}\n\n\ts := searchBoxStyle\n\tif width > 0 {\n\t\t// Border (2) + padding (2) reduce the inner content width.\n\t\ts = s.Width(width - 4)\n\t}\n\treturn s.Render(prompt + text)\n}",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Search is wired in. Summary of the new behavior:\n\n**Keys (letters freed for search):**\n- `↑`/`↓` — navigate the filtered list\n- `←`/`→` (or `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`) — switch tabs\n- Any printable character — appended to the search query\n- `Backspace` — delete last char; `Esc` — clear query\n- `Enter` — launch selected repo\n- `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+Q` — quit\n\n**Filtering:** `orderedRepos(query)` does a case-insensitive substring match on the alias, then applies the existing active-first ordering. When the query changes, `setQuery` resets the cursor to the top so the selection stays valid. Empty results show \"No matches.\"; no repos at all still shows \"No repos yet.\"\n\n**Layout:** a bordered search box (with a 🔍 prompt and a block cursor) sits between the panel and the footer, spanning the width. Placeholder text \"search…\" shows when empty.\n\nTwo honest caveats to verify with `go run .` (I can't render it):\n- I sized the search input at `width - 4` and the panel at `height - 5`; if the search box or panel overflows or leaves a gap on your terminal, the border/padding constants may need a small tweak. Tell me what you see.\n- The \"cursor\" is a static `▏` glyph appended to the text, not a real blinking terminal cursor. If you want a genuine cursor, bubbletea v2's `View.Cursor` field can position one, but the glyph approach is simpler and needs no coordinate math.\n- The 🔍 emoji is double-width; if it renders oddly in your terminal I can swap it for a plain `/` or `>` prompt.\n\nWant me to adjust any of the sizing, or is this good to test?"
          }
        ]
      }

            "data": "Done — `alt+backspace` now clears the search query, alongside `esc`. Builds and vets cleanly.\n\nOne thing to verify when you run it: terminals don't all report Alt+Backspace the same way. Many send it as `alt+backspace` (which is what bubbletea should surface and what I matched), but some emulators send it as a different sequence (e.g. `ctrl+w`-like, or `alt+\\x7f`). If it doesn't clear in your terminal, tell me what `msg.String()` reports for that keypress and I'll match the exact string — quickest way to check is to temporarily surface unmatched keys, or just tell me your terminal and I'll look up its encoding."

      "version": "v1",
      "kind": "ToolResults",
      "data": {
        "message_id": "0117ef83-eb37-4d58-9740-47c722c8b9cd",
        "content": [
          {
            "kind": "toolResult",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01UhioL9GMGLeUxvcBUzUVwo",
              "content": [
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\ttea \"charm.land/bubbletea/v2\"\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/commands\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/repos\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/session\"\n)\n\n// Tab identifies a top-level view in the UI.\ntype Tab int\n\nconst (\n\tTabRepos Tab = iota\n\tTabChats\n\tTabComingSoon\n)\n\n// tabTitles are the labels shown in the tab bar, in order.\nvar tabTitles = []string{\"Repos\", \"Chats\", \"Coming Soon\"}\n\n// sessionFinishedMsg is sent when a tmux session (run via tea.ExecProcess)\n// exits and the bubbletea program resumes.\ntype sessionFinishedMsg struct {\n\terr error\n}\n\ntype model struct {\n\tactiveTab Tab\n\n\t// Terminal dimensions, updated on every resize.\n\twidth  int\n\theight int\n\n\t// Repos tab state.\n\trepoCursor int\n\tquery      string // current search box contents\n\n\t// launchedAlias is the repo whose session was most recently launched,\n\t// so the cursor can follow it after the list reorders.\n\tlaunchedAlias string\n\n\t// lastErr holds the most recent session error, shown in the footer.\n\tlastErr error\n}\n\nfunc initialModel() model {\n\treturn model{\n\t\tactiveTab: TabRepos,\n\t}\n}\n\n// orderedRepos returns the repos in display order: active sessions first\n// (alphabetical), then the rest (alphabetical), filtered by a case-insensitive\n// substring match against query. This is the single source of truth for the\n// Repos tab, so the cursor index, rendering, and launch all agree.\nfunc orderedRepos(query string) []*repos.Repo {\n\tall := repos.All()\n\tq := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))\n\n\tactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tinactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tfor _, r := range all {\n\t\tif q != \"\" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Alias), q) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif r.Session != nil {\n\t\t\tactive = append(active, r)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tinactive = append(inactive, r)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tbyAlias := func(list []*repos.Repo) {\n\t\tsort.Slice(list, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\t\treturn list[i].Alias < list[j].Alias\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tbyAlias(active)\n\tbyAlias(inactive)\n\n\treturn append(active, inactive...)\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Init() tea.Cmd {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos(m.query) {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"ctrl+q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"shift+tab\", \"left\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"tab\", \"right\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Navigate within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\n\t\t// Clear the search query.\n\t\tcase \"esc\", \"alt+backspace\":\n\t\t\tm.setQuery(\"\")\n\n\t\t// Delete the last search character.\n\t\tcase \"backspace\":\n\t\t\tif m.query != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query[:len(m.query)-1])\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Any single printable character is typed into the search box.\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tif s := msg.String(); len(s) == 1 && s[0] >= 0x20 && s[0] < 0x7f {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query + s)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\n// setQuery updates the search query and resets the cursor to the top of the\n// filtered list so the selection stays valid.\nfunc (m *model) setQuery(q string) {\n\tm.query = q\n\tm.repoCursor = 0\n}\n\n// launchSelectedRepo starts (or attaches to) the tmux session for the repo\n// under the cursor, handing the terminal to tmux via tea.ExecProcess. The\n// bubbletea program is suspended while tmux runs and resumes on exit.\nfunc (m model) launchSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tordered := orderedRepos(m.query)\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos || len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\tif m.repoCursor >= len(ordered) {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = len(ordered) - 1\n\t}\n\n\trepo := ordered[m.repoCursor]\n\n\t// Remember which repo we launched so the cursor can follow it to its\n\t// new position once the list reorders on return.\n\tm.launchedAlias = repo.Alias\n\n\t// Decide whether to create+attach (first launch) or just attach\n\t// (session already exists from a previous launch this run).\n\tvar cmd *exec.Cmd\n\tif repo.Session == nil {\n\t\trepo.Session = session.New()\n\t\tcmd = commands.CreateSession(repo.Session.ID, repo.Path)\n\t} else {\n\t\tcmd = commands.AttachToSession(repo.Session.ID)\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, tea.ExecProcess(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {\n\t\treturn sessionFinishedMsg{err: err}\n\t})\n}\n\n// nextTab / prevTab cycle through the tabs.\nfunc (m model) nextTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) + 1) % len(tabTitles))\n}\n\nfunc (m model) prevTab() Tab {\n\treturn Tab((int(m.activeTab) - 1 + len(tabTitles)) % len(tabTitles))\n}\n\n// moveCursor adjusts the cursor for whichever tab is active.\nfunc (m *model) moveCursor(delta int) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcount := len(orderedRepos(m.query))\n\tnext := m.repoCursor + delta\n\tif next >= 0 && next < count {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = next\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m model) View() tea.View {\n\t// Tab bar across the top.\n\ttabBar := TabBar(tabTitles, int(m.activeTab))\n\n\t// Body for the active tab.\n\tvar body string\n\tswitch m.activeTab {\n\tcase TabRepos:\n\t\tbody = m.renderReposTab()\n\tcase TabChats:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Chats\")\n\tcase TabComingSoon:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Coming Soon\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Wrap the body in a bordered panel that fills the window (minus the\n\t// tab bar, search box, and footer rows), with the content centered inside.\n\tpanelHeight := m.height - 5 // tab bar (1) + search box (3, bordered) + footer (1)\n\tpanel := PanelCentered(body, m.width, panelHeight)\n\n\tsearch := SearchBox(m.query, m.width)\n\n\tfooter := Help(\"↑/↓ navigate · ←/→ tabs · type to search · esc clear · enter open · ctrl+c quit\")\n\tif m.lastErr != nil {\n\t\tfooter = Help(\"session error: \"+m.lastErr.Error()) + \"\\n\" + footer\n\t}\n\n\tcontent := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, tabBar, panel, search, footer)\n\n\t// Take over the whole terminal window.\n\tv := tea.NewView(content)\n\tv.AltScreen = true\n\treturn v\n}\n\n// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos(m.query)\n\tif len(repos.All()) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No matches.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}\n\n// renderPlaceholder is shown for tabs with no content yet.\nfunc (m model) renderPlaceholder(name string) string {\n\treturn muted(name + \" — nothing here yet.\")\n}\n\nfunc CreateProgram() *tea.Program {\n\treturn tea.NewProgram(initialModel())\n}"
                },
                {
                  "kind": "text",
                  "data": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n)\n\n// Palette — change colors here to restyle the whole app.\nvar (\n\tcolorAccent = lipgloss.Color(\"205\") // pink/magenta highlight\n\tcolorMuted  = lipgloss.Color(\"240\") // dim gray\n\tcolorBorder = lipgloss.Color(\"63\")  // panel border\n)\n\n// Shared style definitions. These are the single source of truth for the\n// look of the app; every render site draws from them.\nvar (\n\tactiveTabStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().\n\t\t\tBold(true).\n\t\t\tForeground(lipgloss.Color(\"230\")).\n\t\t\tBackground(colorAccent).\n\t\t\tPadding(0, 2)\n\n\tinactiveTabStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().\n\t\t\t\tFaint(true).\n\t\t\t\tPadding(0, 2)\n\n\tpanelStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().\n\t\t\tBorder(lipgloss.RoundedBorder()).\n\t\t\tBorderForeground(colorBorder).\n\t\t\tPadding(1, 2)\n\n\tselectedRowStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().\n\t\t\t\tBold(true).\n\t\t\t\tForeground(colorAccent)\n\n\trowStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle()\n\n\thelpStyle = lipgloss.NewStyle().Faint(true)\n)\n\n// TabLabel renders a single tab             "kind": "text",
            "data": "Now I have the full picture. Let me first give you my recommendation on structure before splitting anything, since \"one file per component\" isn't quite the right axis for a bubbletea app.\n\n**My recommendation on how to split**\n\nBubbletea's architecture is Model-Update-View, not components. A \"component\" (like the tab bar or search box) isn't a self-contained object here — its *state* lives in the model, its *input handling* lives in `Update`, and its *rendering* lives in `View`/`theme.go`. So splitting purely \"one file per component\" would scatter each component's logic across the same three concerns anyway.\n\nA cleaner split for this codebase is **by responsibility**, which is exactly what you asked `ui.go` to become. I'd suggest:\n\n- **`ui.go`** — just the bubbletea wiring: the `model` struct, `initialModel`, `Init`, `Update`, `View`, and `CreateProgram`. This is the \"initialize and update the UI\" role you want. `Update` and `View` stay here but become thin — they delegate.\n- **`repos_tab.go`** — everything specific to the Repos tab: `orderedRepos` (filter+sort), `launchSelectedRepo`, `renderReposTab`, and the repo-list navigation helpers. This is the biggest chunk of domain logic and the most likely to grow.\n- **`tabs.go`** — the `Tab` type, `tabTitles`, `nextTab`/`prevTab`, and `renderPlaceholder` for the empty tabs.\n- **`search.go`** — search state behavior: `setQuery` and the query-editing logic. (The *rendering* `SearchBox` can stay in theme or move here — see below.)\n- **`theme.go`** — stays as the pure styling layer (styles + render helpers). No change needed.\n\nThat gives `ui.go` a single job, and each tab/feature its own file. As you add the Chats tab later, it becomes `chats_tab.go` and `ui.go` doesn't grow.\n\n**One design decision worth making explicitly:** right now rendering is split awkwardly — `theme.go` has `TabBar`, `RepoRow`, `SearchBox` (styled *primitives*), while `ui.go` has `renderReposTab`, `renderPlaceholder` (which *assemble* primitives using model state). That's actually a reasonable boundary: theme = stateless styled primitives; the `render*` methods = model-aware assembly. I'd keep that boundary and just move the `render*` methods next to their tab logic. So `SearchBox` stays in `theme.go` (stateless primitive), but `setQuery` moves to `search.go`.\n\nThis is a pure code-move refactor — no behavior change — so I can verify success simply: it must still build and vet, and `gofmt` clean. \n\nDoes this responsibility-based split (rather than strict one-file-per-component) sound right to you? If so I'll do the moves: `ui.go` slimmed to bubbletea wiring, plus `tabs.go`, `repos_tab.go`, and `search.go`."
          }
        ]
      }

            "data": "Now `repos_tab.go` — ordering/filtering, launch, navigation, and repos rendering:"

          {
            "kind": "toolUse",
            "data": {
              "toolUseId": "toolu_bdrk_01XMLNv4N4bunLnJHhtVSaRA",
              "name": "write",
              "input": {
                "__tool_use_purpose": "Create repos_tab.go holding the Repos tab domain logic and rendering.",
                "command": "create",
                "content": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\t\"os/exec\"\n\t\"sort\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\n\ttea \"charm.land/bubbletea/v2\"\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/commands\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/repos\"\n\t\"github.com/hampusgrimskar/taco/session\"\n)\n\n// orderedRepos returns the repos in display order: active sessions first\n// (alphabetical), then the rest (alphabetical), filtered by a case-insensitive\n// substring match against query. This is the single source of truth for the\n// Repos tab, so the cursor index, rendering, and launch all agree.\nfunc orderedRepos(query string) []*repos.Repo {\n\tall := repos.All()\n\tq := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))\n\n\tactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tinactive := make([]*repos.Repo, 0, len(all))\n\tfor _, r := range all {\n\t\tif q != \"\" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Alias), q) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif r.Session != nil {\n\t\t\tactive = append(active, r)\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tinactive = append(inactive, r)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tbyAlias := func(list []*repos.Repo) {\n\t\tsort.Slice(list, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\t\treturn list[i].Alias < list[j].Alias\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\tbyAlias(active)\n\tbyAlias(inactive)\n\n\treturn append(active, inactive...)\n}\n\n// moveCursor adjusts the cursor for whichever tab is active.\nfunc (m *model) moveCursor(delta int) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcount := len(orderedRepos(m.query))\n\tnext := m.repoCursor + delta\n\tif next >= 0 && next < count {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = next\n\t}\n}\n\n// launchSelectedRepo starts (or attaches to) the tmux session for the repo\n// under the cursor, handing the terminal to tmux via tea.ExecProcess. The\n// bubbletea program is suspended while tmux runs and resumes on exit.\nfunc (m model) launchSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tordered := orderedRepos(m.query)\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos || len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn m, nil\n\t}\n\tif m.repoCursor >= len(ordered) {\n\t\tm.repoCursor = len(ordered) - 1\n\t}\n\n\trepo := ordered[m.repoCursor]\n\n\t// Remember which repo we launched so the cursor can follow it to its\n\t// new position once the list reorders on return.\n\tm.launchedAlias = repo.Alias\n\n\t// Decide whether to create+attach (first launch) or just attach\n\t// (session already exists from a previous launch this run).\n\tvar cmd *exec.Cmd\n\tif repo.Session == nil {\n\t\trepo.Session = session.New()\n\t\tcmd = commands.CreateSession(repo.Session.ID, repo.Path)\n\t} else {\n\t\tcmd = commands.AttachToSession(repo.Session.ID)\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, tea.ExecProcess(cmd, func(err error) tea.Msg {\n\t\treturn sessionFinishedMsg{err: err}\n\t})\n}\n\n// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab() string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos(m.query)\n\tif len(repos.All()) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No matches.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\trows := make([]string, len(ordered))\n\tfor i, repo := range ordered {\n\t\trows[i] = RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i)\n\t}\n\treturn lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n}\n",
                "path": "/Users/egriham/repos/misc/taco/ui/repos_tab.go"
              }
            }
          }
        ]

                "command": "create",
                "content": "package ui\n\nimport (\n\ttea \"charm.land/bubbletea/v2\"\n\t\"charm.land/lipgloss/v2\"\n)\n\n// sessionFinishedMsg is sent when a tmux session (run via tea.ExecProcess)\n// exits and the bubbletea program resumes.\ntype sessionFinishedMsg struct {\n\terr error\n}\n\ntype model struct {\n\tactiveTab Tab\n\n\t// Terminal dimensions, updated on every resize.\n\twidth  int\n\theight int\n\n\t// Repos tab state.\n\trepoCursor int\n\tquery      string // current search box contents\n\n\t// launchedAlias is the repo whose session was most recently launched,\n\t// so the cursor can follow it after the list reorders.\n\tlaunchedAlias string\n\n\t// lastErr holds the most recent session error, shown in the footer.\n\tlastErr error\n}\n\nfunc initialModel() model {\n\treturn model{\n\t\tactiveTab: TabRepos,\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Init() tea.Cmd {\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc (m model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {\n\tswitch msg := msg.(type) {\n\tcase tea.WindowSizeMsg:\n\t\tm.width = msg.Width\n\t\tm.height = msg.Height\n\n\tcase sessionFinishedMsg:\n\t\t// tmux exited (user detached or session ended); bubbletea resumed.\n\t\t// The launched repo has moved to the top, so follow it with the cursor.\n\t\tm.lastErr = msg.err\n\t\tif m.launchedAlias != \"\" {\n\t\t\tfor i, repo := range orderedRepos(m.query) {\n\t\t\t\tif repo.Alias == m.launchedAlias {\n\t\t\t\t\tm.repoCursor = i\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tm.launchedAlias = \"\"\n\t\t}\n\n\tcase tea.KeyPressMsg:\n\t\tswitch msg.String() {\n\n\t\t// Quit.\n\t\tcase \"ctrl+c\", \"ctrl+q\":\n\t\t\treturn m, tea.Quit\n\n\t\t// Switch tabs.\n\t\tcase \"shift+tab\", \"left\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.prevTab()\n\t\tcase \"tab\", \"right\":\n\t\t\tm.activeTab = m.nextTab()\n\n\t\t// Navigate within the active tab.\n\t\tcase \"up\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(-1)\n\t\tcase \"down\":\n\t\t\tm.moveCursor(1)\n\n\t\t// Launch / attach the selected repo's tmux session.\n\t\tcase \"enter\":\n\t\t\treturn m.launchSelectedRepo()\n\n\t\t// Clear the search query.\n\t\tcase \"esc\", \"alt+backspace\":\n\t\t\tm.setQuery(\"\")\n\n\t\t// Delete the last search character.\n\t\tcase \"backspace\":\n\t\t\tif m.query != \"\" {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query[:len(m.query)-1])\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t// Any single printable character is typed into the search box.\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tif s := msg.String(); len(s) == 1 && s[0] >= 0x20 && s[0] < 0x7f {\n\t\t\t\tm.setQuery(m.query + s)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn m, nil\n}\n\nfunc (m model) View() tea.View {\n\t// Tab bar across the top.\n\ttabBar := TabBar(tabTitles, int(m.activeTab))\n\n\t// Body for the active tab.\n\tvar body string\n\tswitch m.activeTab {\n\tcase TabRepos:\n\t\tbody = m.renderReposTab()\n\tcase TabChats:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Chats\")\n\tcase TabComingSoon:\n\t\tbody = m.renderPlaceholder(\"Coming Soon\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Wrap the body in a bordered panel that fills the window (minus the\n\t// tab bar, search box, and footer rows), with the content centered inside.\n\tpanelHeight := m.height - 5 // tab bar (1) + search box (3, bordered) + footer (1)\n\tpanel := PanelCentered(body, m.width, panelHeight)\n\n\tsearch := SearchBox(m.query, m.width)\n\n\tfooter := Help(\"↑/↓ navigate · ←/→ tabs · type to search · esc clear · enter open · ctrl+c quit\")\n\tif m.lastErr != nil {\n\t\tfooter = Help(\"session error: \"+m.lastErr.Error()) + \"\\n\" + footer\n\t}\n\n\tcontent := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, tabBar, panel, search, footer)\n\n\t// Take over the whole terminal window.\n\tv := tea.NewView(content)\n\tv.AltScreen = true\n\treturn v\n}\n\nfunc CreateProgram() *tea.Program {\n\treturn tea.NewProgram(initialModel())\n}\n",

            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Good catch — this is a viewport/scrolling problem. Right now `renderReposTab` renders every row unconditionally, so a list taller than the panel's inner height overflows the box (and the terminal). The fix is to render only the slice of rows that fits, and scroll that window as the cursor moves.\n\nLet me think through the pieces:\n\n1. **Know the visible height.** The panel's inner height is `panelInner(width, panelHeight)`'s height. `renderReposTab` needs that number to know how many rows it can show. Currently it doesn't receive it — I'll pass it in.\n\n2. **Windowing logic.** Given the cursor index and the visible height, compute a scroll offset so the cursor stays in view: if the cursor moves above the window, scroll up; below, scroll down. Standard \"keep cursor visible\" clamp.\n\n3. **Centering interaction.** There's a conflict: `PanelCentered` vertically centers the body. If the list scrolls, centering a full-height list block is odd — a scrolled list should fill the panel top-to-bottom, not be centered. So for the Repos tab I should render the list to exactly the inner height (top-aligned) and *not* vertically center it, while the placeholder tabs can stay centered. I'll handle that distinction in `View`.\n\nLet me look at how `View` computes the panel height and inner area so I pass consistent numbers.\n\nThe panel height is `m.height - 5`, and inner height is that minus border(2)+padding(2) = `m.height - 9`. Let me implement: add a scroll offset to the model, make `renderReposTab` take the visible height and window the rows, and adjust `View` to render the repos body at full inner height (top-aligned) rather than centered.\n\nFirst, add the visible-height helper and window logic to `repos_tab.go`:"

                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "// renderReposTab draws the repo menu with active sessions first, each marked\n// by an indicator aligned in a column to the right of the longest alias. Only\n// visibleRows rows are drawn; the window scrolls to keep the cursor in view.\nfunc (m model) renderReposTab(visibleRows int) string {\n\tordered := orderedRepos(m.query)\n\tif len(repos.All()) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No repos yet.\")\n\t}\n\tif len(ordered) == 0 {\n\t\treturn muted(\"No matches.\")\n\t}\n\n\t// Find the longest alias so the indicator column aligns, then place the\n\t// indicator 5 positions to the right of it.\n\tlongest := 0\n\tfor _, repo := range ordered {\n\t\tif len(repo.Alias) > longest {\n\t\t\tlongest = len(repo.Alias)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\t// Compute the scroll window so the cursor stays visible.\n\tstart, end := scrollWindow(m.repoCursor, len(ordered), visibleRows)\n\n\trows := make([]string, 0, end-start)\n\tfor i := start; i < end; i++ {\n\t\trepo := ordered[i]\n\t\trows = append(rows, RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i))\n\t}\n\n\t// Scroll hints when there are rows off-screen above/below.\n\tbody := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, rows...)\n\tif start > 0 {\n\t\tbody = muted(\"  ↑ more\") + \"\\n\" + body\n\t}\n\tif end < len(ordered) {\n\t\tbody = body + \"\\n\" + muted(\"  ↓ more\")\n\t}\n\treturn body\n}\n\n// scrollWindow returns the [start, end) slice of item indices to display so\n// that the cursor is visible within a window of at most size rows. If size is\n// non-positive, all items are shown.\nfunc scrollWindow(cursor, total, size int) (int, int) {\n\tif size <= 0 || total <= size {\n\t\treturn 0, total\n\t}\n\n\t// Reserve a row for each scroll hint that will be shown, so the windowed\n\t// content plus hints still fits the available height.\n\thalf := size / 2\n\tstart := cursor - half\n\tif start < 0 {\n\t\tstart = 0\n\t}\n\tend := start + size\n\tif end > total {\n\t\tend = total\n\t\tstart = end - size\n\t\tif start < 0 {\n\t\t\tstart = 0\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn start, end\n}",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds, vets, and gofmt-clean. Here's what changed:\n\n**Windowing/scrolling in `renderReposTab`:**\n- It now takes `visibleRows` (the panel's inner height, computed in `View` via `panelInner`).\n- If the list fits, it shows everything. If not, it renders only the slice that fits and reserves 2 rows for scroll hints.\n- `scrollWindow` computes a `[start, end)` slice that keeps the cursor centered-ish and always visible — scroll up when the cursor goes above the window, down when below.\n- `↑ more` / `↓ more` hints appear when there are rows off-screen in that direction.\n\n**Layout in `View`:**\n- The repos list uses `Panel` (top-aligned, fixed size) so it fills the box top-down and never exceeds it.\n- The empty Chats/Coming Soon tabs keep `PanelCentered` since centering makes sense for a short placeholder.\n\nSo the list is now clamped to the blue box and scrolls as you move `↑`/`↓` past the visible edge.\n\nCaveats to check with `go run .` (I can't render it):\n- The row-count math assumes each repo is exactly one line and the \"more\" hints one line each. That holds here. If a very small terminal makes `panelHeight` tiny or negative, `innerHeight` could go non-positive — `scrollWindow` guards `size <= 0` by showing all (which could overflow on an extremely short window). If you want, I can add a hard floor so nothing renders below a minimum viable height.\n- I reserve 2 hint rows whenever scrolling is active, even at the very top (where only `↓ more` shows) — so there may be one blank row at the top edge in that case. It never overflows; it's at most one row of slack. I can make the reservation exact (1 or 2 depending on position) if the slack bothers you.\n\nWant me to tighten the hint-row reservation to be exact, or is the current behavior fine?"
          }
        ]
      }

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "That's because of how `scrollWindow` computes the start: it does `start = cursor - half`, which tries to keep the cursor in the *middle* of the window. So as soon as you move past the midpoint, it starts scrolling to re-center. That's the \"always centered\" scroll style.\n\nWhat you want is the more common \"scroll only at the edges\" style: the window stays put until the cursor actually reaches the top or bottom visible row, and only then does it scroll by one to follow. Let me rewrite `scrollWindow` for that behavior.\n\nThe catch: edge-scrolling needs to know the *current* window position to decide whether to nudge it, but `scrollWindow` is called fresh each render with only the cursor. I can make it stateless by deriving the window purely from the cursor with edge semantics — but true edge-scrolling requires remembering the previous offset. The clean fix is to store the scroll offset in the model and adjust it when the cursor moves, rather than recomputing from scratch.\n\nLet me do it properly: add a `repoScroll` offset to the model, adjust it in `moveCursor` (and when the query changes), and have the renderer just use it."
          },

                "__tool_use_purpose": "Replace centered scrolling with edge-based scrolling using a persistent offset.",
                "command": "strReplace",
                "newStr": "// visibleRepoRows returns how many repo rows fit in the panel's inner height\n// for the current terminal size.\nfunc (m model) visibleRepoRows() int {\n\tpanelHeight := m.height - 5\n\t_, innerHeight := panelInner(m.width, panelHeight)\n\tif innerHeight < 1 {\n\t\treturn 1\n\t}\n\treturn innerHeight\n}\n\n// moveCursor adjusts the cursor for whichever tab is active, scrolling the\n// repo list only when the cursor would move past a visible edge.\nfunc (m *model) moveCursor(delta int) {\n\tif m.activeTab != TabRepos {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcount := len(orderedRepos(m.query))\n\tnext := m.repoCursor + delta\n\tif next < 0 || next >= count {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tm.repoCursor = next\n\tm.clampScroll(count)\n}\n\n// clampScroll nudges the scroll offset so the cursor stays within the visible\n// window, scrolling only at the edges. It reserves rows for scroll hints so\n// the visible content plus hints fits.\nfunc (m *model) clampScroll(total int) {\n\tvisible := m.visibleRepoRows()\n\trows := visibleItemRows(total, visible)\n\n\t// Scroll up if the cursor is above the window.\n\tif m.repoCursor < m.repoScroll {\n\t\tm.repoScroll = m.repoCursor\n\t}\n\t// Scroll down if the cursor is at/below the bottom visible row.\n\tif m.repoCursor >= m.repoScroll+rows {\n\t\tm.repoScroll = m.repoCursor - rows + 1\n\t}\n\t// Keep the offset in range.\n\tmaxScroll := total - rows\n\tif maxScroll < 0 {\n\t\tmaxScroll = 0\n\t}\n\tif m.repoScroll > maxScroll {\n\t\tm.repoScroll = maxScroll\n\t}\n\tif m.repoScroll < 0 {\n\t\tm.repoScroll = 0\n\t}\n}\n\n// visibleItemRows returns how many item rows are shown given the total item\n// count and the available height, reserving rows for scroll hints when the\n// list does not fully fit.\nfunc visibleItemRows(total, visible int) int {\n\tif total <= visible {\n\t\treturn visible\n\t}\n\trows := visible - 2 // reserve for top + bottom hints\n\tif rows < 1 {\n\t\trows = 1\n\t}\n\treturn rows\n}",

                "newStr": "\tindicatorCol := longest + 5\n\n\ttotal := len(ordered)\n\trows := visibleItemRows(total, visibleRows)\n\n\t// Window using the persistent scroll offset; clamp defensively in case the\n\t// terminal was resized since the last cursor move.\n\tstart := m.repoScroll\n\tif start > total-rows {\n\t\tstart = total - rows\n\t}\n\tif start < 0 {\n\t\tstart = 0\n\t}\n\tend := start + rows\n\tif end > total {\n\t\tend = total\n\t}\n\n\tlines := make([]string, 0, end-start)\n\tfor i := start; i < end; i++ {\n\t\trepo := ordered[i]\n\t\tlines = append(lines, RepoRow(repo.Alias, indicatorCol, repo.Session != nil, m.repoCursor == i))\n\t}\n\n\t// Scroll hints when there are rows off-screen above/below.\n\tbody := lipgloss.JoinVertical(lipgloss.Left, lines...)\n\tif start > 0 {\n\t\tbody = muted(\"  ↑ more\") + \"\\n\" + body\n\t}\n\tif end < total {\n\t\tbody = body + \"\\n\" + muted(\"  ↓ more\")\n\t}\n\treturn body\n}",

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Builds, vets, and gofmt-clean. The scrolling now works the way you expected:\n\n- The window **stays fixed** as you move down until the cursor reaches the **bottom visible row**. Only then does moving down scroll the list by one. Same at the top going up. No more re-centering as you cross the midpoint.\n- This is done with a persistent `repoScroll` offset in the model. `moveCursor` moves the cursor first, then `clampScroll` nudges the offset only if the cursor left the visible window at an edge.\n- `setQuery` resets the scroll to top when filtering, and the post-launch cursor jump re-clamps it.\n\nRoot cause of the old behavior: the previous `scrollWindow` computed `start = cursor - half`, which is a \"keep cursor centered\" strategy — inherently scrolls at the midpoint. I replaced it with edge-triggered scrolling backed by a stored offset, which is the standard list-viewport behavior.\n\nVerify with `go run .` on a list taller than the box: move down and confirm nothing scrolls until you hit the last visible row, then it follows one row at a time.\n\nOne note: `visibleRepoRows` recomputes from `m.height` each time, so it stays correct across terminal resizes; the renderer also defensively re-clamps `start`, so a resize between a keypress and a redraw can't push the window out of range."
          }
        ]
      }
    },
    {

          {
            "kind": "text",
            "data": "Right — the box changes height because `Panel` sizes itself to its content, and the body's line count varies as hints appear/disappear. Wait, actually `Panel` sets a fixed `.Height()`, so the border should stay put... but Lip Gloss's `.Height()` sets a *minimum* — if the content is *taller* than that height, the box grows. That's the bug: when both hints show, the body can exceed the inner height by a line, pushing the box taller.\n\nThe real fix is to make the body **always exactly `innerHeight` lines**, regardless of whether hints are present. Two things to guarantee:\n\n1. The item rows + hint rows must sum to exactly the visible height (never more, never fewer).\n2. When there aren't enough items to fill the height, pad with blank lines so the box doesn't shrink either.\n\nThe cleanest approach: always reserve fixed slots for the hint rows (top and bottom), show either the hint or a blank line in each slot, and pad the item area to a fixed count. That way the total line count is constant. Let me restructure `renderReposTab` to produce a fixed-height block."
          },
